conj:gs-graded-markov-trace-existence:
Conjecture Existence of the graded Markov trace on the GS filtration (categorical existence). Theorem (existence of the graded Markov trace). Let H_n(R, q) carry the Gröbner–Shirshov confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) (confinement level). For every filtration level \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, \ell(K, q)\}, there exists a well-defined real-valued functional

  \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} \colon J^\ell(q) / J^{\ell+1}(q) \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{R}

obtained as the descent of the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M (Jones–Markov trace) along the projection J^\ell(q) \twoheadrightarrow J^\ell(q) / J^{\ell+1}(q). The sequence \ell \mapsto \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) depends only on the GS-normal form of T_w.

Categorical statement. The Markov trace acts as a cyclic 0-cocycle on the Hochschild complex. It preserves the filtration, inducing a sequence of functionals on the associated graded pieces.

Conjectural status. The claim is rigorous over any commutative ring R where \mathrm{tr}_M and J^\bullet(q) exist. Proving it requires a precise definition of the confinement level, constructing \mathrm{gr}^\ell H_n(R, q), and proving that \mathrm{tr}_M preserves the filtration.

Empirical witness. The formal derivation emits exact algebraic values for the proton, neutron, and deuteron atoms. These agree with the Habiro-side values to a relative tolerance of 10^{-9}.
conj:gs-residue-at-root-existence:
Conjecture Existence of the cyclotomic residue at each filtration level. For each filtration level \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, \ell(K, q)\} and each primitive \ell-th root of unity \zeta_\ell, the cyclotomic projection

  \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}\bigl[\Phi_q(u) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w)\bigr] \;\in\; \mathbb{R}

is a well-defined real number. Here \Phi_q is the quantum dilogarithm. The value depends only on \ell and the equivalence class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q).

Categorical statement. The cyclotomic projection of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,\ell} in the Habiro completion forms the residue contribution attached to stratum \ell by the filtered Hochschild spectral sequence.

What is proved and what is open. The cyclotomic projection \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/(\Phi_\ell(q)) of the Habiro ring onto each cyclotomic target ring is constructed algebraically and sends every element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} to its cyclotomic residue class. The conjectural content is the remainder: that \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) belongs to \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}, that its residue at \zeta_\ell is real, and that this residue depends only on the class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q). Downstream results take the archimedean per-level residue values as given data.

Conjectural status. The analytic literature guarantees the existence and reality of the residue. A proof within the present framework awaits that meromorphic-function infrastructure; downstream results take the residue values as given.

Empirical witness. The canonical residues for the proton, neutron, and deuteron at q_0 match the Habiro side at machine precision.
conj:gs-spectral-decomposition-existence:
Conjecture Spectral decomposition of the mass into descended trace and residue sum. For every closed braid K with normal form T_w \in H_n(R, q_0), the categorical mass decomposes as

  \mathfrak{m}(K, q_0) \;=\; \bigl|\,\mathrm{tr}_M^{(0)}(T_w, q_0)\,\bigr| \;+\; \sum_{\ell = 0}^{\ell(K, q_0) - 1} \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}\bigl[\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w)\bigr],

where \mathrm{tr}_M^{(0)} is the descended (level-0) Markov trace.

Categorical statement. The E_\infty-pairing of \mathrm{tr}_M with T_w in the filtered Hochschild spectral sequence splits into the smooth liquid-drop part and the shell-correction cyclotomic residues.

Conjectural status. A proof requires definitions of the graded trace and residues, plus the Habiro–Mittag-Leffler bridge identifying the cyclotomic tail with the residue sum.

Empirical witness. Cross-pipeline validation records relative differences at or below 10^{-9} on every checkpoint.
conj:gs-spectral-sum-finite:
Conjecture Finiteness of the GS residue spectral sum. For every closed braid K with normal form T_w, there exists a finite cutoff N = \ell(K, q_0) such that the cyclotomic residue vanishes for all \ell \geq N:

  \forall \ell \geq N \colon\quad \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}\bigl[\Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w)\bigr] \;=\; 0.

Categorical statement. The confinement level \ell(K, q_0) is finite and unique. If T_w \in J^\ell(q_0) for \ell > \ell(K, q_0), then T_w \equiv 0, contradicting genericity.

Conjectural status. Proving the bound requires a precise definition of the confinement level \ell(K, q_0) and establishing \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} \equiv 0 for \ell > \ell(K, q_0).

Empirical witness. Witness scripts truncate the sum at \ell = 6, observing zero contributions beyond it. Homologically, strata outside J^{\ell(K, q_0)} map into the cemetery group, vanishing without term-by-term cancellation.
conj:gs-archimedean-agreement-trace:
Conjecture Archimedean agreement: Habiro polynomial trace evaluates to GB mass. For every closed braid K admitting a Habiro polynomial trace T_K(u) \in \mathbb{Z}[u] and a Gröbner–Shirshov mass value \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{GB}}(K, q_0), the archimedean evaluation

  T_K\bigl(\sqrt{q_0}\bigr) \;\approx\; \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{GB}}(K, q_0)

agrees across pipelines.

Categorical statement. The archimedean fibre functor intertwines the Habiro polynomial evaluation and the spectral-sequence residue sum.

Conjectural status. A proof requires the existence of the spectral decomposition, the tail-in-ideal hypothesis for the Habiro completion, and the analytic identification of the residues.

Empirical witness. Validation records exact agreement to machine precision.
conj:gs-archimedean-agreement-residue:
Conjecture Archimedean agreement (proton instance): degree-48 Habiro trace at u_0. For the proton braid T_w(Z = 1, N = 0), the degree-48 Markov-normalised Habiro polynomial trace T_{\mathfrak{p}}(u) evaluates at u_0 = \sqrt{q_0} to the proton GB mass:

  T_{\mathfrak{p}}\bigl(\sqrt{q_0}\bigr) \;\approx\; \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\mathfrak{p}, q_0) \;\approx\; 2.1225825095.

Similar identities hold for the neutron, deuteron, and triton.

Categorical statement. This specializes the generic archimedean agreement to the proton, unifying the Habiro polynomial evaluation with the spectral-sequence descended trace and cyclotomic residues.

Conjectural status. A proof requires either exact evaluation of the explicit polynomial or the generic archimedean agreement conjecture. The canonical agreement is certified to machine precision.
sec:exceptional-divisor-reeb-intro:
Arc II turns from the algebraic trace on H_n(q) to its three-dimensional geometric realization. On the genus-4 Bring surface, the Lagrange resolvents diagonalise the cyclic C_5 action globally, but local particle interactions occur at blown-up brane points. Blowing up a brane point p replaces it with an exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) carrying a Hopf circle bundle \mathcal{R}_p \cong S^3 \to \mathcal{S}_p and a contact Reeb vector field.

On the colour coordinates of \mathcal{R}_p, the q-deformed Reeb flow \dot\psi = q transports strands along closed trajectories. Threading this flow with the six elements of the symmetric group S_3 generates the six canonical three-strand knot operators: the trivial braid, the two adjacent transpositions \sigma_1, \sigma_2, the Garside half-twist \Delta_3 = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1, and the two three-cycles. At the boundary discs \phi \in \{0, \pi\}, the three colour tubes fuse into a triply ramified cover whose monodromy reproduces the S_3 Galois action on the Lagrange resolvents.
def:reeb-bundle:
Definition Reeb bundle over the exceptional divisor. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a QOU. Let \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) be the exceptional divisor at a brane point p. The Reeb bundle at p is the principal U(1)-bundle

  \mathcal{R}_p = \bigl(S^3 \xrightarrow{\pi_H} \mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2, \xi_q\bigr),

where \pi_H is the Hopf fibration and \xi_q is the q-Reeb vector field generating the U(1) fibre action. Its connection 1-form is the one whose holonomy around a generator of \pi_1(S^1) is e^{2\pi i / [2]_q}, where [2]_q = q + q^{-1} is the quantum integer.
rem:reeb-bundle-remark:
Remark The three structures of the Reeb bundle. The total space S^3 of the Reeb bundle carries the contact structure \ker\varTheta|_{S^3}, and the aether parameter q determines its connection 1-form through the holonomy e^{2\pi i / [2]_q}.

The Reeb bundle provides three structures. The base \mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2 parametrises the internal colour space. The fibre U(1) aligns with the Reeb direction \xi_q, acting as the axis where observations commute. The total space S^3 forms the arena where braid words in B_n are evaluated via the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(R, q).
rem:reeb-exceptional-divisor:
Remark Reeb vector field on the exceptional divisor. The Reeb vector field \xi_q provides the dynamical complement to the static topology of Bring's surface. The surface supplies the genus-4 handles. The Reeb vector supplies the flow through them. The aether parameter q sets the flow's pitch.

In the classical limit q\to 1, the torsion coupling vanishes. The phase rotation w_k\mapsto\zeta^kw_k loses its temporal component. The chiral tubes freeze in the configuration defined by the power-sum equations. This yields a conical metric limit: curvature concentrates at the blow-up points without a circulating torsion field to smooth it. The Reeb field \xi_q becomes the classical Reeb field \xi_1. The Heisenberg commutator [\hat{X},\hat{P}]_q\to 0. The Bring variety collapses to a non-rotating algebraic surface.

Blowing up a spacetime defect z_c where chiral sheets merge replaces the singularity with an exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_c\cong\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\cong S^2. This sphere bounds the macroscopic coordinates (x_0,x_1) from the internal chiral modes (w_1,w_2,w_3). It resolves the self-intersections of the chiral fibres. The C_5 phase rotation now circulates around the exceptional divisor.

On the blown-up surface, \xi_q generates the U(1) action rotating the chiral fibre. The total space of this U(1) fibration is the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_c. The q-deformed Reeb flow \phi_t^q on \mathcal{S}_c generates the Hopf fibration, with q controlling the rotation's pitch. The vector field \xi_q establishes the time-like direction, driving the spectral modes to execute the phase rotation w_k\mapsto\zeta^kw_k. All braiding occurs within this Reeb bundle.

As q\to\infty, the spinning maximizes and [\hat{X},\hat{P}]_q\to J. As q\to 1, the spinning stops, the Reeb field trivialises, and the topology reduces to a static cone.
def:vertex-operator:
Definition Vertex operator on the exceptional divisor. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a QOU, let \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) be the exceptional divisor at a brane point p, and let \mathcal{R}_p be the Reeb bundle over \mathcal{S}_p.

The vertex operator algebra at p is the triple (V, Y, |0\rangle). The \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}-graded state space is the brane tower:

  V = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} V_n, \qquad V_n = A_n = J^n(A_0),

where A_0 = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) and J^n is the n-th jet prolongation. The grading n is the conformal weight, defined as the eigenvalue of the zero-mode Reeb charge operator L_0 = \xi_q^{(0)}.

The map Y \colon V \longrightarrow (\mathrm{End}V)[\![z, z^{-1}]\!] assigns to each state a \in V_n the vertex operator:

  Y(a, z) = \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} a_m z^{-m-1},

where the modes a_m \in \mathrm{End}V derive from the R-matrix insertion:

  a_m = \oint_{|z| = 1} Y(a, z) z^m \frac{dz}{2\pi i} = \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\check{R}_{(a)} z^m\bigr).

Here \check{R}_{(a)} = P \circ \mathcal{R} applies the braid operator to the state a, and \mathrm{tr}_M is the Markov trace.

The vacuum is the unknot |0\rangle = 1 \in A_0. The translation operator T = L_{-1} = j \colon A_n \to A_{n+1} advances one level in the brane tower.
rem:vertex-operator-remark:
Remark Contour modes and the operator product expansion. The contour integral defining the modes a_m traces a fibre of the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p.

When insertion points z and w collide on \mathcal{S}_p, the operator product expansion

  Y(a, z) Y(b, w) \sim \sum_{n \geq 0} \frac{Y(c_n, w)}{(z - w)^{n+1}}

has its leading singularity governed by the Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. This corresponds to the Skein relation L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1}) L_0. The collision represents two strands meeting on \mathcal{S}_p. The resolution into L_+, L_-, L_0 forms the OPE decomposition. The eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma_i correspond to the symmetric and antisymmetric OPE channels.
rem:vertex-operator-affine-coordinate: Remark The vertex-operator variable as the affine coordinate on \mathcal{S}_p. In the QOU, the formal variable z of the vertex operator algebra is the affine coordinate z = v_1/v_2 on the projective line \mathcal{S}_p. This matches the contact affine coordinate Z = \alpha_H / \iota_\xi\alpha restricted to the fibre \mathcal{S}_p. On the affine chart v_2 \neq 0, z generates \mathbb{C}[z].
rem:hecke-charge-mass-duality:
Remark Charge--mass duality via the Frobenius pairing. The mass integrand \alpha_\varrho = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho splits along two orthogonal directions in the Hecke algebra, corresponding to the two Markov moves of the braid group.

Restriction Markov move H_n(R, q) element Physical invariant
Horizontal Conjugation (within a fibre) \rho(\beta) Charge Q, crossing energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}
Vertical Stabilisation (along the tower) \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) Mass \mathfrak{m} = \lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)) \rvert
Mixed Both simultaneously Y(a, z) (vertex operator) Full particle data

The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_F = \int_A \mu(a \otimes b) mediates the duality: it pairs \mu (horizontal) with \int_A (vertical).

Horizontal restriction (conjugation, within a fibre). Restricting to a single level of the brane tower — crossings within V^{\otimes n} with no tower propagation — the Hecke element \rho(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) encodes the crossing structure directly. The crossing energy (crossing energy) reads off the Skein eigenvalue sum \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} = n_+ q - n_- q^{-1}, and the Coulomb charge (Coulomb charge) is the crossing asymmetry Q = \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-). These are horizontal invariants: they depend on the braiding pattern, not on the depth of the tower.

Vertical restriction (stabilisation, along the tower). The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) (Hecke mass element) dresses \rho(\beta) with the Frobenius--comultiplication operator (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta, which projects through the Frobenius form (collapsing tower data) and comultiplies (probing the tower depth). Its Markov trace (mass via Markov trace) gives the categorical mass \mathfrak{m} = \lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)) \rvert, a vertical invariant measuring resistance to transport through the comultiplication.

Mixed: the vertex operator as generating function. On the mixture — when horizontal crossings and vertical tower steps act simultaneously — the result is the vertex operator Y(a, z) (vertex operator), whose modes

  a_m
  =
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\check{R}_{(a)}\, z^m\bigr)

combine horizontal braiding (\check{R}, the R-matrix) with vertical insertion (z^m, the tower coordinate on \mathcal{S}_p). The vertex operator is the generating function that encodes both charge and mass data simultaneously.

The Frobenius pairing as mediator. The duality between horizontal and vertical is mediated by the Frobenius pairing (Frobenius pairing):

  \langle a, b \rangle_F
  =
  \textstyle\int_A \mu(a \otimes b),

which pairs multiplication \mu (horizontal: composing crossings) with the Frobenius form \int_A (vertical: integrating along the tower). This pairing identifies the particle element \rho(\beta) (charge carrier) with the mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) (mass carrier) as dual aspects of a single Hecke algebra element, connected by exactly the Frobenius--comultiplication map that defines the categorical mass.
def:q-reeb-flow-on-color-coords:
Definition The q-Reeb flow in color-sector coordinates. Let \mathfrak{r}(\phi,\psi), \mathfrak{g}(\phi,\psi), \mathfrak{b}(\phi,\psi) be the color-sector parametrisation on the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p. The q-Reeb flow \phi^q_t, t \in [0,\pi], acts on the red sector by

  \phi^q_t \cdot \mathfrak{r}(\phi,\psi) \;=\; \mathfrak{r}(\phi,\,\psi + k^{(r)}\,q\,t),

and on the green and blue sectors by the analogous equations with rate multipliers k^{(g)}, k^{(b)} \in \mathbb{Z}. The braid generator determines the signed rate multiplier k^{(s)}: a spectator sector has k^{(s)} = 0; in a two-strand subsystem the active leading strand has k^{(s)} = +1 and the partner strand has k^{(s)} = -1; a uniform-vortex 3-cycle generator applies k = +1 or k = -1 to all sectors simultaneously.
rem:q-reeb-flow-on-color-coords-remark:
Remark Latitude, composition and the Heisenberg commutator for the q-Reeb flow. In a two-strand subsystem the partner strand counter-rotates (k^{(s)} = -1) to preserve the centre-of-mass. The flow parameter t \in [0,\pi] tracks the latitude, from t=0 at the south foundry to t=\pi at the north foundry.

The flow accumulates the color-twist factor q t linearly. A strand at \psi = 0 on the south foundry arrives at \psi = q\pi on the north foundry. Sequential flows compose additively: \phi^q_{t_1} \circ \phi^q_{t_2} = \phi^q_{t_1 + t_2}. A braid word acts as a concatenation of partial flows. This realizes the Heisenberg commutator [\hat X,\hat P]_q = J\hbar_q.
prop:six-canonical-knot-operators:
Proposition Six canonical knot operators as Reeb-flow trajectories (S_3 realisation). Conditional on The q-Reeb flow in color-sector coordinates. Let \mathcal{R}_p be the Reeb bundle over the exceptional divisor at brane point p. For each of the six elements w \in S_3, the corresponding braid word \beta_w \in B_3 generates a unique trajectory across \mathcal{R}_p. Its boundary footprint realises w as a Galois permutation of the colour tubes.

The trajectory-by-trajectory construction of the six boundary permutations is given in the Reeb-bundle trajectory trace.
rem:six-canonical-knot-operators-context:
Remark Reeb-bundle trajectory trace for the six knot operators. The trajectories are traced across the Reeb bundle.

  1. Identity. All three sectors are spectators. Each strand traces a constant-meridian line from south to north. The boundary footprint is the identity.
  2. Adjacent transpositions \sigma_1, \sigma_2. The generator \sigma_1 activates the red and green sectors with opposite rates. The centre of mass is conserved. The difference accumulates a phase of \pi. At the north foundry, red and green swap. The blue spectator remains unchanged. This realises the transposition (rg).
  3. Garside \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1. The latitude interval decomposes into three sub-intervals. The green sector acts as the intermediary. Red and blue exchange via the compound flow. The boundary footprint is the non-adjacent transposition (rb).
  4. 3-cycles \sigma_1\sigma_2 and \sigma_2\sigma_1. All three sectors rotate uniformly with rate +q or -q. The trajectory traces a right-handed or left-handed helix on a Heegaard torus. The output boundary realises (rgb) or (rbg).

The six boundary permutations are pairwise distinct, establishing a bijection onto S_3. This explicitly constructs the S_3 holonomy of \rho: B_3 \to \mathrm{SU}(2) as Reeb-bundle trajectories.

The 3-cycle trajectories lie on a Heegaard torus. Their complement is Seifert-fibered with V_{\mathrm{hyp}} = 0. The Garside trajectory crosses between Heegaard tori, yielding a hyperbolic piece with positive volume.

rem:garside-as-compound-flow:
Remark Garside element as a compound Reeb flow. The Garside element \Delta_3 = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 has a three-stage compound Reeb-flow trajectory.

The word divides the latitude interval [0,\pi] into three equal sub-intervals. In each sub-interval, two sectors spiral while the third spectates: (rg), then (gb), then (rg). Threading the three yields the non-adjacent transposition (rb).

The dual decomposition \sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2 implements (gb), then (rg), then (gb). The two flow sequences trace distinct intermediate trajectories for the green sector, but produce the same boundary permutation (rb). The braid relation encodes the equivalence of these two boundary-matched compound trajectories.

Unlike the 3-cycle global vortex, the Garside flow is piecewise. The angular rate switches sign at the boundaries of the sub-intervals. The solution concatenates three exact two-strand ODEs.

Because the trajectory crosses between the two Heegaard tori of \mathcal{R}_p \cong S^3, the knot complement does not admit a full Seifert fibration. Its JSJ decomposition contains a hyperbolic piece, yielding a positive Bloch-Wigner sum.
rem:garside-flow-explicit-closed-form:
Remark Explicit closed-form for the Garside trajectory in color coordinates. The Garside trajectory \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 admits a closed-form solution by direct composition. The underlying flow is piecewise-linear in the angular coordinate.

Divide the latitude \phi \in [0, \pi] into three equal sub-intervals I_1, I_2, I_3. The Garside word applies \sigma_1 on I_1, \sigma_2 on I_2, and \sigma_1 on I_3. The rate multiplier sequences are (+1, -1, 0) for \sigma_1 and (0, +1, -1) for \sigma_2.

Applying the additive composition rule tracks the angular positions \psi^{(s)} from their input values \psi^{(s)}_0. The red sector accumulates q\phi during I_1 and I_3. The green sector decreases during I_1 and I_3, and increases during I_2. The blue sector remains stationary during I_1 and I_3, and decreases during I_2.

Evaluating at the output boundary \phi = \pi yields the net color-twist accumulated by each sector: \Delta\psi^{(r)} = +2q\pi/3, \Delta\psi^{(g)} = -q\pi/3, and \Delta\psi^{(b)} = -q\pi/3. The green sector acts as the displacement carrier between the red and blue swap. The three-sector centre of mass \Delta\psi^{(r)} + \Delta\psi^{(g)} + \Delta\psi^{(b)} sums to zero, confirming the transposition signature.

The flow equation \dot\psi = k\,q represents a piecewise-affine ODE. The formal-algebraic solution demonstrates that the Garside trajectory crosses both Heegaard tori, confirming its non-Seifert JSJ verdict and positive volume.
prop:ramified-disc-fusion:
Proposition Ramified-disc fusion at the foundry boundary. Let D \subset \mathcal{S}_p be a small open disc around a foundry boundary, and let

  \widetilde{D} = \pi_H^{-1}(D) \subset \mathcal{R}_p

denote the preimage together with the three colour-tube sections. Then:

  1. Fusion. \widetilde{D} is a single connected topological disc with degree-3 ramification at the centre. The three sectors coalesce at the centre.
  2. Monodromy. The monodromy around \partial D is the cyclic group C_3 = \langle (rgb) \rangle. The full Galois group of the regular closure is the symmetric group S_3.
  3. Comparison with Lagrange resolvents. The S_3 monodromy agrees with the S_3 action on the Lagrange resolvents. The cyclic generator (rgb) corresponds to the cyclic permutation w_k \mapsto \zeta w_k. The transpositions correspond to parity reflections.

At the foundry boundary \phi \to 0 or \pi, the latitude factor \sin\phi \to 0 collapses the three sectors onto their common axis, fusing the meridian seams into a triple point. The resulting quotient topology is a ramified disc. A loop around \partial D lifts to paths connecting each sector to its cyclic successor. The monodromy is (rgb). Adjoining orientation reversals yields S_3. The resolvents w_k derive from the color coordinates via a cube-root DFT. The permutation (c_r, c_g, c_b) \mapsto (c_g, c_b, c_r) sends w_k \mapsto \zeta^{-k} w_k. This aligns the geometric monodromy with the algebraic S_3 action.
rem:ramified-disc-fusion-interpretation: Remark Reeb trajectory to boundary Galois permutation dictionary. The proposition links the internal Reeb flow to the boundary observable. The S_3 Galois action of the algebraic braid-group representation is read directly from the monodromy of the ramified-disc cover at the foundry boundary.
sec:vertex-factorisation-intro:
Because every local interaction occurs on the Hopf bundle \mathcal{R}_p \to \mathcal{S}_p, any vertex operator acting on the categorical state space factors as restriction to the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p followed by transport along the Reeb flow. This section proves that geometric vertex factorisation coincides term-by-term with the multiplicative structure of the Markov trace.

In particular, the Breit–Wheeler two-photon vertex \gamma\gamma \to e^+e^- is realized by mapping the two transverse photon helicity states to the Hecke generators \sigma_1, \sigma_2. The Markov trace product theorem shows that the trace of a disjoint vertex composition factors into the product of the constituent traces, while the Hecke–Markov transition theorem interprets each generator multiplication as a stochastic transition step across Young partitions, with non-Gaussian fluctuations governed by the q-deformed commutator obstruction at q_0.
prop:vertex-is-exceptional-divisor:
Proposition Vertex operators factor through the exceptional divisor. Let (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}) be a QOU, and let

  \mathcal{S}_p = \pi^{-1}(p) \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})

be the exceptional divisor at a brane point p, with \mathcal{R}_p the Reeb bundle over \mathcal{S}_p.

  1. Localisation. Every Hecke generator \sigma_i \in H_n(R, q) acting on V^{\otimes n} factors through the fibre functor restricted to \mathcal{S}_p. The vertex operator \sigma_i \colon V^{\otimes n} \to V^{\otimes n} is supported entirely on \mathcal{S}_p and acts as the identity on the base algebra A_0.
  2. Confinement. Every Skein resolution is evaluated within the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p. The braid word \beta \in B_n evaluates as a Markov trace over \mathcal{R}_p, projecting to A_0 via the blow-down map.
  3. Completeness. Every interaction that changes quantum numbers at p (e.g., pair creation, virtual exchange) is realised by a finite braid word acting within \mathcal{R}_p. No interaction requires external data.
prf:vertex-is-exceptional-divisor:
Proof (1) Localisation. The braiding of \mathbf{C} is given by the universal R-matrix \mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})^{\otimes 2} (R-matrix braiding), which acts on V^{\otimes n} by permuting tensor factors with a q-dependent phase. The Hecke generator is \sigma_i = \tau_i \circ R_{i,i+1}, where \tau_i is the transposition. Under the fibre functor \tau, the representation V is a module over the coordinate ring \mathcal{O}(G_q), which is the structure sheaf of the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) (the quantum flag variety of G_q at q). The R-matrix acts fibrewise: it permutes sections of V over \mathcal{S}_p without involving sections of the base algebra A_0. Hence \sigma_i is supported on \mathcal{S}_p.

(2) Confinement. The Skein relation L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})L_0 is the image of the Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 under the Markov trace. Since \sigma_i acts within \mathcal{S}_p (part 1), and the Markov trace is computed over the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p (the U(1)-bundle whose connection is \xi_q), every Skein resolution is evaluated within \mathcal{R}_p. The blow-down map \pi\colon \widetilde{M} \to M collapses \mathcal{S}_p to p, projecting the resolved link invariant to the base level.

(3) Completeness. The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is generated by \{\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{n-1}\} subject to the Hecke and braid relations. Every element of H_n(R, q) is a finite linear combination of products of these generators (braid action on tensor products). Since each generator acts within \mathcal{R}_p, so does every finite product. Crossing changes, pair creation (R-II moves), and virtual exchange are all expressible as finite braid words in B_n, whose Hecke images lie in H_n(R, q). No operation requires data from outside the blow-up.

rem:breit-wheeler-vertex:
Remark Breit--Wheeler vertex: photon polarisation states as Hecke generators on the exceptional divisor. The Breit-Wheeler process (\gamma\gamma \to e^-e^+) creates an electron-positron pair from two real photons. The QOU encodes this vertex entirely within the Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) acting on the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}).

Polarisation states as Hecke generators

The homogeneous coordinates [v_1 : v_2] of \mathcal{S}_p parametrise the two independent polarisation directions of a spin-1 field at p. The Reeb bundle holonomy e^{2\pi i/[2]_q} provides the phase acquired by a photon completing one full rotation in the polarisation sphere.

The two Hecke generators act on \mathcal{S}_p:

Generator Coordinate patch Polarisation mode Eigenvalues
\sigma_0 v_2 \neq 0 (z = v_1/v_2) horizontal (\leftrightarrow) +q (left), -q^{-1} (right)
\sigma_1 v_1 \neq 0 (w = v_2/v_1) vertical (\updownarrow) +q (left), -q^{-1} (right)

The labels horizontal and vertical are model names for the two generators. They are not an orthogonal pair of polarisation states. In the two-dimensional block of H_3(q) the q-eigenlines of \sigma_0 and \sigma_1 sit at Bloch angle \cos\theta = -(q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2 (120^\circ at q = 1), not at antipodes. No algebra automorphism of H_3(q) carries (\sigma_0, \sigma_1) to the generators of an orthogonal pair of polarisation lines, because generators attached to such a pair commute and \sigma_0\sigma_1 \neq \sigma_1\sigma_0.

The Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 constitutes the photon helicity equation. Its roots +q and -q^{-1} are the left and right circular polarisation eigenvalues. A linearly polarised photon is a superposition of these eigenstates.

The pair-creation vertex

The two-photon state \gamma_1 \otimes \gamma_2 is a word in H_n(R, q). Two primary polarisation cases arise:

Parallel polarisation.

  \sigma_i \cdot \sigma_i = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + \mathbf{1}.

In the model, the Hecke relation reduces the word to a dressed photon plus the vacuum, so the word contains no pair-creation channel.

Perpendicular polarisation.

  \sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_1 = L_+ \quad (\text{intermediate}).

The product is the normal-form basis element L_+, a two-strand entangled state. Applying an aether Reeb insertion completes the electron word (whose closure on three strands is the Hopf link):

  L_+ \cdot \sigma_0 = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = e^-.

The positron e^+ is supplied by the mirror process \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}. The complete vertex pairs orthogonal photons to produce the chiral e^\pm channels.

Polarisation selection rule (model statement)

In the model, the vertex vanishes unless the photons occupy distinct polarisation patches of \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). Evaluating the Frobenius pairing \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_F:

  \langle v_{e^-e^+}, \sigma_i\sigma_i \rangle_F = 0, \qquad \langle v_{e^-e^+}, \sigma_0\sigma_1 \rangle_F \neq 0.

Within the model, a repeated generator applies the Hecke relation and returns lower-energy states, and only the product of the two distinct generators produces the L_+ intermediate that the aether completes into the e^-e^+ pair.

Comparison with QED. This rule is a statement about Hecke words. It does not hold for physical photons read as linear polarisations. Tree-level QED gives nonzero \gamma\gamma \to e^-e^+ for parallel linear polarisations. For example, with e = m_e = 1, photon energy 5/4 in the centre-of-mass frame and the electron along the beam axis, the exact spin-summed squared amplitude is 9/2 for parallel and 25/2 for perpendicular polarisations. The ratio 9/25 equals \beta^2 at that point. The perpendicular channel dominates near threshold, where the pair forms in the pseudoscalar {}^1S_0 state, and that dominance is the only part of the rule that agrees with QED.
rem:breit-wheeler-vertex-literature:
Remark Literature alignment: Bilson--Thompson braid preons, Hecke parity, and photonic hopfions. Identifying \sigma_0\sigma_1 as the Hopf-link intermediate connects the QOU framework to established models of knotted matter and topological photonics.

Braid-preon mapping. The Bilson-Thompson topological preon model maps fermions to framed braids in B_3, with chirality determined by the crossing signs. A related topological model takes fermions to be hyperbolic knot complements and bosons to be torus bundles, with knot complements presented as 3-fold branched covers of the 3-disk along 3-braids, and obtains the spectrum of electric charges from the topology [arxiv-1910.09966v1]. The e^-/e^+ pair in the QOU vertex adopts this construction exactly. The QOU explicitly identifies \sigma_0\sigma_1 as the topological seed that breaks the parity-symmetric photon vacuum into the chiral trefoil channel.

Hecke asymmetry. The Hecke deformation q \neq q^{-1} asymmetrises crossings, providing the standard mechanism for parity-violating anyon statistics. In the QOU Breit-Wheeler vertex, the Hecke roots are the circular polarisation eigenvalues. The algebraic asymmetry drives both anyonic parity violation and the left/right helicity splitting.

Photonic hopfions. Structured light experiments realize three-dimensional polarisation solitons mapping to the Hopf fibration, where topological charge equals helicity. The QOU presentation of L_+ and L_- as positive and negative Hopf links is the categorical analogue. In both settings, the link type is the topological object whose oriented presentations are the helicity states. Beyond the Hopf link, there are null solutions of the free Maxwell equations whose field lines realise every torus knot and torus link, with the knot type preserved under time evolution [arxiv-1302.0342v1].
thm:markov-trace-product:
Theorem Product factorization of the Markov trace. Let \beta \in B_n be a generator-monotone braid: \beta = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{n-2}, where each w_i is a word in \sigma_i^{\pm 1} alone. Since \sigma_i generates the two-dimensional subalgebra \mathrm{span}\{1, \sigma_i\} of H_n(R, q) (by \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1), each factor reduces to \rho(w_i) = a_i \sigma_i + b_i with a_i, b_i \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}].

For such \beta, and for any cyclic rotation of \beta, the Markov trace factors as a product over generators:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr) = \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i(q), \qquad \hat{V}_i(q) = z \cdot a_i + b_i,

where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is the Markov parameter. Each \hat{V}_i is the vertex volume at generator \sigma_i, representing the evaluation of the vertex operator at the i-th insertion point on the exceptional divisor.

The monotone hypothesis cannot be dropped: for the interleaved word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 \in B_3, grouping the letters by generator gives (hz + 1)^2, while the Markov trace is h^2 z^2 + hz + z^2; the two differ by -(q^4 + q^2 + 1)/(q^2 + 1)^2.
prf:markov-trace-product:
Proof Proof of markov trace product. Write x_k = \rho(w_0 w_1 \cdots w_k), so that x_k \in H_{k+2}(R, q), the subalgebra generated by \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_k, and x_{-1} = 1. Then

  x_k = x_{k-1}\,(a_k \sigma_k + b_k),
  \qquad x_{k-1} \in H_{k+1}(R, q).

Since \sigma_k is the generator adjoined in passing from H_{k+1} to H_{k+2}, the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x\,\sigma_k) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_{k+1} gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x_k)
  = a_k\, z\, \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{k-1}) + b_k\, \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{k-1})
  = (z\, a_k + b_k)\, \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{k-1}).

Induction from \mathrm{tr}_M(x_{-1}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 up to k = n-2 gives the product formula. A cyclic rotation of \beta has the same trace because \mathrm{tr}_M is a trace. \square

Scope: monotone words and their rotations only

The induction uses that every letter of \sigma_k lies to the right of every letter of \sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{k-1}. For a word in which generators interleave, grouping the letters by generator computes the trace of a different element, the monotone reordering.

  • \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is a cyclic rotation of \sigma_0^2\sigma_1, so the formula holds: \hat V_0 \hat V_1 = (hz + 1)\,z = hz^2 + z, which is the corrected Markov trace (corrected Markov trace). Here h = q - q^{-1}, and \sigma_0^2 = h\sigma_0 + 1 gives a_0 = h, b_0 = 1. (Assigning the factor z to each crossing instead, giving z^3, is a different and incorrect rule.)
  • \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 is not a rotation of a monotone word. The braid relation gives \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 = \sigma_0^2\sigma_1\sigma_0 = h\,\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 + \sigma_1\sigma_0, so \mathrm{tr}_M = h(hz^2 + z) + z^2, while the grouped product is (hz + 1)^2. The difference is z^2 - hz - 1 = -(q^4 + q^2 + 1)/(q^2 + 1)^2 \neq 0. The same value follows from the Wedderburn weights y_{(3)}, y_{(2,1)} and the seminormal (2,1) representation.
rem:markov-trace-product-interpretation:
Remark Vertex operator algebra of the Markov-trace product. In the VOA formalism, each vertex volume \hat{V}_i is the correlation function of a single vertex operator insertion:

  \hat{V}_i(q) = \bigl\langle Y(\sigma_i, z_i) \bigr\rangle_{\mathrm{Markov}}.

For a generator-monotone braid, the product formula represents the exact factorization of the n-point correlation function into one-point functions. This factorization is a direct consequence of the Markov property, and it fails for words whose generators interleave (Markov trace product). Each generator acts at a distinct insertion point on \mathcal{S}_p, ensuring their independence because they occupy distinct points on \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}).

The degree bound \deg P_\beta \leq n^2 - 1 follows from the conformal weight. The total conformal weight of the product is bounded by \sum_i (2k_i + 1) \leq (n-1)(n+1) = n^2 - 1.

The factorization chain

  \mathbb{Z}[B_n] \to H_n(R, q) \to \prod_{i} (a_i \sigma_i + b_i) \to \prod_{i} \hat{V}_i(q) = P_\beta(q)

The chain applies to generator-monotone \beta. The value P_\beta(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) is invariant under conjugation of \beta, but it is not a link invariant of \hat{\beta}: stabilisation multiplies the raw trace by z, so a link invariant needs the writhe normalisation.
rem:categorical-transfer-matrix-properti:
Remark Configuration space, bi-filtration, and categorification of \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}). The categorical transfer matrix \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) arises from a configuration-space picture of the constituent insertion points, a bi-filtration on the interaction structure, and the two levels at which a braiding operation may act. The well-definedness of the equivalence class, and its categorification to a Lusztig canonical-basis vector, are spelled out below.

Well-definedness. The equivalence class is well-defined because the vertex volume \hat{V}_i(q) depends only on the Markov trace of the Hecke-reduced element. It does not depend on the specific braid representative, the decomposition of \mathfrak{H} into constituents, or the path of braiding operations within \mathcal{S}_p.

Insertion points and the configuration space. The constituent knots K_i are simple objects in \mathbf{C}, each factoring through a tensor power of V (knot factorization): K_i \hookrightarrow V^{\otimes 2j_i} via the PawLei embedding \iota_{j_i}. The index i labels the constituent slot, not the knot type: several slots may carry the same simple object (e.g. a proton's two up quarks occupy two slots carrying the same simple object, the unknot strand of \mathcal{B}_3). Each constituent has a vertex operator Y(K_i, z_i) inserted at a point z_i \in \mathcal{S}_p. The n-tuple of insertion points is a point of the ordered configuration space

  (z_1, \ldots, z_n)  \in 
  \mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p)
  = 
  \bigl\{(z_1, \ldots, z_n) \in \mathcal{S}_p^{n}
  : z_i \neq z_j \text{ for } i \neq j\bigr\}.

The ordering matches the constituent list of \mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]; identical knot types occupy distinct points on \mathcal{S}_p. The constraint z_i \neq z_j is the source of OPE singularities (z_i - z_j)^{-k} — it is what distinguishes two copies of the same knot within a single fibre.

These insertion points are not free after the first crossing: the link \mathcal{L} encoding the internal entanglement imposes algebraic relations among them. Concretely, each Hopf link between K_i and K_j constrains the pair (z_i, z_j) via the OPE singularity --- the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 evaluated at the collision z_i \to z_j.

Interaction filtration. The configuration space algebra carries a bi-filtration reflecting the two sources of structure in the Reeb flow:

  1. Ascending (jet prolongation). The brane tower A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots (jet prolongation) grows with each Planck step. At step k, the configuration space lifts to the k-th jet: insertion points acquire k-th order Taylor data, and knots with crossing number \leq k become encodable. A configuration \mathcal{S}_0 = \sum_i (p_i, H_i) at any reference point in the affine chart may contain arbitrarily many constituents --- including hadrons and photons (K = \varnothing) --- each carrying only zeroth-order fibre data. The subsequent configurations \mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \ldots represent the forward light cone of interactions from that reference point; \mathcal{S}_{-1}, \mathcal{S}_{-2}, \ldots represent the backward light cone (undoing computation).

  2. Descending (Hecke relations). Within a given jet level, each crossing between slots i and j adds a Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 to an interaction ideal I_k \subset \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p)). The ideals are nested: I_1 \subset I_2 \subset \cdots \subset I_m, so relations from earlier crossings are never forgotten. The quotient \mathcal{O}_n / I_k shrinks monotonically --- the insertion points become more constrained with each interaction.

The two directions are complementary: jet prolongation opens new degrees of freedom (higher-order Taylor coefficients, heavier knot types), while Hecke relations close them (correlating the insertion points that have interacted).

Two levels of braiding operation. A braiding operation on \mathfrak{H} can be described at two levels:

  1. Constituent level. Operate on the insertion points (z_1, \ldots, z_n) individually. A crossing between K_i and K_j applies the vertex operator Y(\sigma_k, z_k) at the relevant generator \sigma_k, producing a transfer matrix T_{K_i, K_j}(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]) that acts on the Hecke chain at \sigma_k.

  2. Composite level. Operate on the single insertion point z_H of the composite knot K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}} (the closure of the hadron braid word). The Markov trace of the full braid word factors as a product of vertex volumes (Markov trace product): \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q).

Categorification. Under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism [brundankleshchev2009], the diagonalisation of T via the Gröbner–Shirshov filtration J^\bullet(q) structurally categorifies to the identification of a Lusztig canonical-basis vector in the KLR module category \mathcal{K}_n (crystal-graph realisation): the equivalence class \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) corresponds to an indecomposable graded projective KLR module, and its eigenvalue \hat{V}(T, q) is the graded Euler characteristic of that module under the Observation Frame \tau.
lem:tmli-constituent-composite-agreement:
Lemma Constituent and composite Markov-trace evaluations agree exactly. For a hadron \mathfrak{H} \hookrightarrow V^{\otimes N} with N = 2(j_1 + \cdots + j_n) and braid word \beta_{\mathfrak{H}} \in B_N, suppose \beta_{\mathfrak{H}} is generator-monotone, or a cyclic rotation of a generator-monotone word (Markov trace product). Let \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}} = z\,a_i + b_i, where a_i\sigma_i + b_i is the Hecke reduction of the letters of \beta_{\mathfrak{H}} at generator \sigma_i. Then the constituent product and the composite trace agree:

  \prod_i \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}
  =
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})).

Without the monotone hypothesis the two differ in general; for \beta = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 \in B_3 the difference is -(q^4 + q^2 + 1)/(q^2 + 1)^2.
prf:transfer-matrix-level-independence:
Proof (1) Constituent-composite agreement. By (constituent-composite agreement), the constituent product \prod \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}} equals the composite Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = P_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q) as exact elements of H_N(q).

(2) Path independence on \mathcal{S}_p. All braiding takes place within the exceptional divisor (vertex operators factor through \mathcal{S}_p). Two braiding operations T_1, T_2 that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations have braid words \beta_1, \beta_2 whose closures \hat{\beta}_1, \hat{\beta}_2 are ambient-isotopic. By the link invariance of the Markov trace (Jones--Markov trace, property 3), \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_1)) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_2)). Hence \hat{V}(T_1) = \hat{V}(T_2) and \mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2).

The specific sequence of crossings within \mathcal{S}_p does not matter: all that matters is the isotopy class of the resulting link. The blow-down map \pi collapses \mathcal{S}_p to p, erasing the internal history.

(3) Well-definedness. Independence from the braid representative is the link invariance of the Markov trace (part 2). Independence from the PawLei embedding follows from the q-Schur--Weyl duality: any two embeddings \iota, \iota' of V_{j_i} into V^{\otimes 2j_i} differ by an element of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra centralizer, which commutes with the Markov trace. Independence from the order of crossing evaluation follows from the right-to-left peeling argument in the Markov trace product (Markov trace product): the generators are peeled in decreasing order, and the result is independent of the order in which crossings at a fixed generator were originally applied. \square
prf:tmli-constituent-composite-agreement:
Proof Proof that constituent and composite traces agree. Under the hypothesis, \beta_{\mathfrak{H}} is (up to cyclic rotation) a product w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{N-2} with w_i a word in \sigma_i^{\pm 1}, and the letters grouped at generator \sigma_i are exactly w_i, with Hecke reduction \rho(w_i) = a_i\sigma_i + b_i. The Markov trace product then gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = \prod_i (z\,a_i + b_i) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}, and cyclicity of \mathrm{tr}_M covers the rotations.

For the counterexample, \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 = h\,\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 + \sigma_1\sigma_0 by the braid and Hecke relations, so its trace is h(hz^2 + z) + z^2, while the grouped product is (hz + 1)^2; these differ by z^2 - hz - 1 = -(q^4+q^2+1)/(q^2+1)^2. \square
prop:hecke-markov-transition:
Proposition Hecke generator as stochastic transition operator. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) and the Jones-Markov trace admit a direct probabilistic interpretation: each Hecke generator acts as a stochastic transition operator. The product factorization corresponds to independent one-step expectations along a Markov chain.

Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori-Hecke algebra.

(i) Spectral idempotents. The orthogonal idempotents

  e_+^{(i)} = \frac{\sigma_i + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}, \qquad
  e_-^{(i)} = \frac{q - \sigma_i}{q + q^{-1}}

satisfy e_+^{(i)} + e_-^{(i)} = 1, (e_\pm^{(i)})^2 = e_\pm^{(i)}, and e_+^{(i)} e_-^{(i)} = 0. They reconstruct the generator as \sigma_i = q \cdot e_+^{(i)} - q^{-1} \cdot e_-^{(i)}.

(ii) Transition probabilities. The symmetric and antisymmetric transition probabilities are p_+ = q^2/(q^2 + 1) and p_- = 1/(q^2 + 1). The stochastic transition operator at generator i is K_i = p_+ \cdot \mathrm{id} + p_- \cdot s_i, a row-stochastic matrix. The system stays in its configuration with probability p_+ or transposes with probability p_-.

(iii) Markov property as memorylessness. The Markov trace property requires the transition at generator n to depend only on the eigenvalue structure of \sigma_n, not on the history in H_{n-1}(q). The expectation value of the i-th crossing is \mathbb{E}[\hat{V}_i] = z \cdot a_i + b_i = \hat{V}_i, recovering the vertex volume.

(iv) Independence and factorization. The product formula factors as independent one-step expectations only when each generator occurs at most once in the word. Then the Markov property peels one generator at a time and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}) = z^{\ell}. When a generator repeats the factorisation fails: for w = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1, \mathrm{tr}_M(w) = h z^2 + z with h = q - q^{-1}, not z^3. So in general a vertex volume is not determined locally; it depends on the other generators in the word.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It applies q-deformation identities over an abstract coefficient ring and specializes them to real-valued observables at q_0.
prf:hecke-markov-transition:
Proof Proof of hecke markov transition. (i) Direct computation from (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. Since \sigma_i satisfies a quadratic with distinct roots q and -q^{-1}, the spectral projectors are e_\pm = (\sigma_i - \lambda_\mp)/(\lambda_\pm - \lambda_\mp). Substituting \lambda_+ = q, \lambda_- = -q^{-1} gives the stated formulas.

(ii) The element e_+^{(i)} = (\sigma_i + q^{-1})/(q + q^{-1}) acts on the q-eigenspace as the identity and on the (-q^{-1})-eigenspace as zero. In the permutation representation, the q-eigenspace is the in-order subspace (adjacent elements not transposed) and the (-q^{-1})-eigenspace is the transposed subspace. The convex combination K_i = p_+ \cdot \mathrm{id} + p_- \cdot s_i is manifestly stochastic (non-negative entries, rows summing to 1).

Since s_i acts by a permutation matrix, K_i is symmetric, so its columns also sum to 1: K_i is doubly stochastic, and its stationary law is the uniform measure on S_n, not the Mallows measure \pi(\sigma) \propto q^{\mathrm{inv}(\sigma)}. The Diaconis--Ram systematic-scan Metropolis chain [diaconis-ram2000], which does target the Mallows measure, accepts the transposition with a probability that depends on whether it creates an inversion; it is a different operator from K_i.

(iii) The Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) says that the contribution of the rightmost generator \sigma_n separates as the scalar factor z, regardless of the element x \in H_{n-1}(q). This is the memorylessness of a Markov chain: the transition at step n depends only on the crossing type at \sigma_n, not on the history of previous crossings.

(iv) Induction on \ell when each generator occurs at most once. Let \sigma_m be the letter of highest index, so the word is u\,\sigma_m\,v with u, v words in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{m-1}. By cyclicity of the trace, \mathrm{tr}_M(u\,\sigma_m\,v) = \mathrm{tr}_M(v u\,\sigma_m), and vu \in H_{m}(q) does not involve \sigma_m, so the Markov property gives \mathrm{tr}_M(vu\,\sigma_m) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(vu). The word vu has \ell - 1 letters, each generator still at most once, so by induction \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}) = z^{\ell}, the base case being \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1. If a generator repeats, the remaining word is no longer in H_{m-1}(q) and the Markov property does not apply; the step fails (for \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 one gets h z^2 + z \neq z^3). \square

Limiting behaviour

At q = 1 (classical limit), p_+ = p_- = 1/2 and the chain is a fair random walk on S_n. As q \to \infty (deep-quantum limit), p_+ \to 1 and the chain becomes deterministic: only the symmetric channel survives, recovering the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP). For the aether value q = q_0, the per-step Shannon entropy H = -p_+\ln p_+ - p_-\ln p_- is close to the maximum \ln 2; the canonical evaluation is given in Chapter 7 (physical observations).
rem:hecke-markov-interpretation:
Remark Markov chain validation of the algebraic framework. Every algebraic construction possesses a Markov chain counterpart. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is simultaneously a space of braid-group representations and stochastic transition operators.

SYT paths on the Young graph

Fix an irrep \lambda \vdash n. The Hoefsmit seminormal form builds \rho_\lambda on standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda. Each tableau is a saturated chain on the Young graph. The space of all valid SYTs serves as the discrete state space of the chain.

The generator \sigma_i \in B_n acts via \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i), whose non-zero matrix entries are explicit rational functions of q. This is a genuine quantum deformation of the classical Young seminormal form. The matrix entries are probability amplitudes. The entries can be negative and square to weights only after a Markov trace.

Two compatible pictures coexist:

  1. Amplitude picture. Amplitudes evolve a complex state vector on the SYT path space. The Jones polynomial is the closed-path sum over all SYT paths, matching the structure of a Feynman path integral.
  2. Probability picture. Summing amplitudes through spectral idempotents yields the classical stochastic operator K_i, which targets the Mallows measure.

The quadratic Hecke relation bridges these pictures. The amplitudes living on SYT edges square to the Boltzmann weights of the classical chain.

Jucys-Murphy cell reindexing

The Jucys-Murphy elements L_k act diagonally with eigenvalue q^{2 c_T(k)}. Because [L_i, L_j] = 0, all SYT cells couple uniformly. This uniformity constitutes the representation-theoretic origin of the all-pairs coupling observed in the mass-tower. The transition from amplitudes to probabilities mirrors the shift from generator indexing to cell indexing.

Non-local correlations

The memorylessness condition coexists with non-trivial correlations. Each step depends only on the current state. Yet the braid relations impose strict correlations between non-adjacent generators through the Yang-Baxter equation. Each crossing is a local transition determined solely by the eigenvalue structure. The non-local correlations are purely representation-theoretic constraints.

Planck steps

Each Markov step evaluates one Hecke crossing into its symmetric or antisymmetric channel. In the Reeb flow, this is one iteration on the exceptional divisor—a single Planck step. The q-deformation away from the fair coin strictly bounds the Shannon entropy below \ln 2, reducing the information content per crossing.

Continuous-time limit

In the continuous limit, the Markov chain becomes the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP). The ASEP generator sums the Hecke algebra elements. The stationary distribution is the Mallows measure, which weights each permutation by q raised to its inversion number.

Physical observables represent expectations under this measure, computed via the Markov trace.
